claims.statement: security-chart.svelte owns the chart lifecycle: onMount creates the lightweight-charts instance (CrosshairMode.Normal, transparent layout, formatLocalTime as the time formatter, formatLocalTickMark as the tick-mark formatter, ignoreWhitespaceIndices false, hidden left price scale, right price scale with minimumWidth 75), adds the CandlestickSeries, creates and attaches the ValuationBandPrimitive and calls updatePanes, attaches six further series primitives to that series (UserPriceAlerts, ElliottWavesPrimitive, FibonacciPrimitive, MeasurePrimitive, HorizontalLinePrimitive, FreeFormLinePrimitive) and subscribes their delegates, installs a capture-phase non-passive wheel listener that zooms the price scale, price-scale mouse/pointer drag listeners and a ResizeObserver, and the teardown removes every wheel/mouse/pointer listener, disconnects the observer, destroys the six alert/drawing primitives (not the valuation band) and only then calls chartInstance.remove().

Oscillator indicators do not get separate chart panes: every pane (main, volume, rsi, macd, obv) is a price-scale id whose visible band is carved out with priceScale().applyOptions({scaleMargins}), the stacking order is main, then volume when present, then OSCILLATOR_PANE_IDS (rsi, macd, obv), the ordered ids are held in explicit orderedPaneIds state so imperative add/remove updates them reliably, and the margin arithmetic itself lives in the pure module $lib/chart/indicator-pane-layout.ts which the chart only applies (main via seriesInstance.priceScale(), the rest via chartInstance.priceScale(id)).

Future whitespace keeps drawing ahead of the last candle possible: generateFutureWhitespace returns an empty array for fewer than two candles or a non-positive count, derives the bar interval from the median spacing of the most recent candles via computeIntervalSeconds and appends count whitespace points one interval apart with the reference candle's Time shape preserved; checkAndExpandWhitespace grows the allocated count when the visible range nears the right edge or the container needs more bars and re-applies the previously saved visible logical range so the expansion is invisible to the user.

The candles $effect in security-chart.svelte is the single writer of series data: it no-ops when the candles array reference is unchanged, clears series data and every drawing primitive's candle set for empty input, detects prepended history and shifts the visible logical range by the number of added candles, sizes the whitespace count from futureBars and the container width on first load and then shows the last 250 bars, and on every non-empty update writes the candles plus generated future whitespace and pushes the raw candles into all five drawing primitives.

Drawing mode locks chart panning: one $effect ORs all five drawing flags (wave, fib, measure, horizontal line, free-form line) and applies handleScroll.pressedMouseMove = !isDrawing, and each primitive's drawingModeChanged subscription restores pressedMouseMove = true only once every other drawing flag is off, so finishing one tool does not unlock panning while another is still active.

chart-preferences.ts concentrates the security page's pure chart helpers: mergeChartPreferences preserves the indicators key across partial writes, displayCandlesFor selects Heikin-Ashi or raw candles by chart style, shouldForceRefetch forces or compares intervals, parseCandleTime normalizes every lightweight-charts Time shape to a Date, mergeCandles dedupes incoming candles by String(time) and prepends them, and shouldFetchMoreData guards pagination.

Timeframe handling covers five intervals (1h, 4h, 1d, 1w, 1m): getChartDateWindow returns a 30-day window for intraday intervals and a 2-year window otherwise, intraday prices map to UTCTimestamp epoch seconds while daily and coarser intervals keep date strings, and changeTimeframe persists the timeframe preference outside the fetch try/catch (and only when the fetch succeeded) so a failed preference write can neither mask a fetch error nor hold isChangingTimeframe open.

The security route's server load returns only { security_id } (throwing a 400 when the param is missing) and never fetches the security or its prices; the identity plus a 1d price window are fetched after navigation by SecurityPageDataService, and the page reconciles that always-1d series with the saved timeframe by force-refetching the active selectedInterval when it is not 1d and no timeframe change is already in flight.

Indicator defaults live in one deep-frozen table: INDICATOR_DEFAULTS is key-ordered to match the sidebar render order and deep-frozen so accidental mutation throws, and createIndicatorConfigs() returns entries whose nested settings share no reference with the frozen defaults.

addIndicator composes each indicator type from the right series shape — a volume HistogramSeries on the 'volume' scale, a single LineSeries for rsi, three series for macd (histogram plus MACD and signal lines) sharing the 'macd' scale, a LineSeries with a custom M/1M price formatter on the 'obv' scale, three LineSeries plus a BandsIndicator series primitive attached to the middle band for bb on the main scale, and a plain LineSeries overlay otherwise — while removeIndicator detaches the bands primitive, removes every series of the group and drops any stored custom pane height for that indicator.

Indicator values come from the backend IndicatorsService: the page builds IndicatorSpec requests per enabled indicator and keeps a monotonic sequenceCounter with a per-indicator indicatorSeq map to discard stale responses, volume is rendered locally from the displayed candles, and avgPrice is a dashed price line fed by blendedAverageCost(holdings) rather than an indicator series.

wave-alerts.ts derives and reconciles wave-target alerts: computeWaveAlertLevels iterates degree by target wave deterministically, skips a degree whose percent is null or whose target is missing, rounds each level to 8 decimals to match the backend DECIMAL(16,8) column, sets the condition by comparison with the current price and skips equality; reconcileWaveAlerts diffs existing alerts by (condition, level) and never returns manual alerts (source !== 'wave') for deletion, so a second run over applied state returns empty sets.

The user-price-alerts plugin is deliberately not built on DrawingPrimitiveBase: it has its own MouseHandlers because it needs pointer positions over the price scale that the shared handler clips, exposes both pane views and price-axis pane views, adds an alert at coordinateToPrice(y) when the pointer clicks above the price scale, and removes the hovered alert when its remove button is clicked; its state keeps alerts in a Map with a price-descending array view and 6-digit random ids regenerated on collision.

security-chart bridges the alert primitive to the backend: an $effect pushes alerts into setAlerts as {id: String(id), price: target_price}, alertAdded derives the condition from the last candle close (above when the alert price exceeds it) and calls onAddAlert, and alertRemoved parses the string id back to a number and calls onRemoveAlert.

Wave-target alerts are reconciled against the live alert list: handleWaveSettingsChange and the drawings service's wave-change path schedule a reconcile, the page serializes reconciles on a single promise chain because onWaveChange fires once per placed point, the initial reconcile is gated on preferences having loaded so a failed preference fetch cannot mass-delete wave alerts, and any create or delete triggers loadAlerts().

Chart tests are colocated with their subject and must mock the chart and canvas layers: security-chart.test.ts stubs Path2D and ResizeObserver before importing the component and replaces lightweight-charts with a vi.mock factory of chainable createChart/timeScale/priceScale/addSeries/attachPrimitive mocks, while plugin tests build a fake CanvasRenderingTarget2D whose useBitmapCoordinateSpace invokes the callback with a fake BitmapCoordinatesRenderingScope and a recording 2D context, and every API client a subject calls is mocked.

SecurityPageDataService (page-data.svelte.ts) owns the post-navigation data wave: load(securityId) fetches getSecurity and getPrices for a 1d window with getChartDateWindow in parallel, guards against a stale in-flight load clobbering a newer soft navigation with a private loadSeq, never throws (it returns the caught error so the page can route a 401 through redirectOn401), and treats a missing or empty price items array as a successful load whose message lands in error; the page's per-security $effect resets tool state, timeframeError and pagination, awaits that load, and renders an instant titlebar from the default watchlist plus a Loading chart data placeholder until the chart module resolves.

The pure pane-layout module owns the whole distribution: computeDefaultPaneScaleMargins reproduces the legacy margins exactly (main 0.1/0.1 with no oscillators or volume; volume 0.7/0 and main 0.1/0.35 for volume only; per-oscillator height 0.25/0.18/0.14 by active count with a 0.02 gap and a main-area floor of 0.3, with volume taking the bottom 25% of the main area), computePaneScaleMargins returns those defaults byte-for-byte whenever no custom height applies to a present pane, and with custom heights distributePaneHeights allocates 1 - TOP_MARGIN - BOTTOM_MARGIN - (n-1) * PANE_GAP across panes weighted by the custom height or derived default, clamped to [MIN_PANE_FRACTION 0.08, MAX_PANE_FRACTION 0.8] by a water-filling allocatePaneHeights that pins out-of-bounds panes and redistributes the remainder.

Custom pane heights are interactive in the chart component: it renders one absolutely-positioned resize handle per adjacent pane pair (data-testid pane-resize-handle-<upper>-<lower>) at the boundary between the two margins, a pointer drag converts the vertical delta into a fraction moved between the two panes while preserving their sum and clamping both to [MIN_PANE_FRACTION, MAX_PANE_FRACTION] and re-applies the margins on every move, the window-level pointerup/pointercancel fires onPaneHeightsChange exactly once, a Reset pane sizes button appears only while a custom height applies to a present pane, and removeIndicator deletes the removed pane's stored height so re-adding starts from the default.

Pane heights persist through the indicator_pane_heights user preference: the page's handlePaneHeightsChange updates local userPreferences and PATCHes the whole key (sending null on reset, because PATCH replaces it), and applySavedPaneHeights restores a stored map by calling chartRef.setPaneHeights behind a setTimeout(..., 100) so the chart ref is bound first, no-oping when the stored map is absent or empty.

The indicator compute contract is IndicatorsService.computeIndicators posting { interval, chart_style, indicators: IndicatorSpec[], candles?, from_date?, to_date? } to /api/v1/market/securities/{security_id}/indicators/compute and receiving { indicators: Record<string, unknown[]> } keyed by spec id/type, with the page reading res.indicators[id] ?? res.indicators[spec.type] ?? []; buildIndicatorSpec copies the spec id/type and settings plus only the positive numeric fields period, fast, slow, signal and stdDev.

The backend compute route validates the optional date window (422 when from_date exceeds to_date), builds candles from the daily price repository (aggregating to weekly or monthly when asked) or the intraday repository (aggregating to 4h), or uses request.candles verbatim, converts to Heikin-Ashi server-side when chart_style is heikin_ashi, and delegates to the external indicator service (mapping timeouts to 504 and connection errors or 5xx to 503); the IndicatorCache is read and written only when request.candles is absent, because the cache key is security + interval + chart style + a digest of the canonical indicator specs and date window and cannot describe a caller-supplied candle set.

Indicator responses are guarded against out-of-order arrival on two paths: the bulk refreshActiveIndicators stamps a monotonic sequenceCounter into indicatorSeq for every enabled indicator and accepts each response entry only while that indicator is still enabled and its stored sequence matches, while the single onIndicatorToggle stamps one id and accepts only if the sequence, the enabled flag and the chart ref still agree; disabling an indicator bumps its sequence so an in-flight response cannot resurrect it, and isLoadingIndicators is only cleared by the newest request.

chart-settings-modal.svelte has three sections (general, waves, fibonacci) that each hold local draft state resynced from props through serialized JSON.stringify keys or previous-value comparisons (to avoid spurious resyncs from $state proxies): general persists the hide-labels / auto-scale / log-scale toggles, waves validates the per-degree wave-3/wave-5 percentages and blocks the save on non-numeric, non-finite or negative input before persisting wave_settings, and the fibonacci section is disabled whenever the page reports no active drawing; the modal opens from the toolbar settings button or Cmd/Ctrl+, which ChartDrawingsService.handleKeyDown routes to onChartSettingsOpen.

A single hideLabels $effect drives lastValueVisible, priceLineVisible and title across every indicator series group — the MACD histogram/MACD/signal trio, the BB upper/middle/lower trio and any generic single series — using the indicator's configured label and blanking the titles when labels are hidden.

The exported updateData(candles) is the imperative replacement path for series data: it sets lastCandlesRef so the candle $effect does not re-apply, grows the whitespace count from the container width, writes the candles plus generated future whitespace, and shows the last 250 bars — but it does not push candles into the drawing primitives.

Pagination is driven from the same visible-logical-range subscription: the chart sets isLoadingMore and calls onLoadMoreData when the range starts at or before bar 10, more history exists and no load is in flight, the page's handleLoadMoreData fetches the older window for the active interval, merges it with mergeCandles (dedupe by String(time), prepend) and sets hasMoreData false when the response is empty or adds no new candles, and an $effect clears isLoadingMore as soon as hasMoreData goes false.

A capture-phase, non-passive wheel listener zooms the price scale rather than the time scale: when the pointer x falls inside the price-scale strip (container width minus the price scale width, falling back to 75 px) it prevents default and propagation and scales the price scale's visible range span by 1.025 on scroll down or 0.975 on scroll up around the range mid-point (in log coordinates when logScale is on); wheel events over the chart canvas are left alone.

sparkline.svelte is a chart-library-free SVG sparkline used by the holdings views: it derives values from plain numbers or Candle.close, builds a Catmull-Rom smoothed line plus a closed area path inside a fixed 0 0 100 height view box with a gradient fill, and colors by an explicit color/isPositive or by first-versus-last trend; it never touches lightweight-charts.

Charting tests cover the surface at three levels: indicator-pane-layout.test.ts pins the legacy default margins for 0/1/2/3 oscillators and the volume variants, custom-height normalization, min/max clamping and the water-filling allocator; indicator-defaults.test.ts pins the frozen default table, its sidebar key order and copy independence; security-chart.test.ts covers oscillator panes and custom price scales, hideLabels, the price-scale wheel zoom and drag, the drawing pan-lock restore rules, future whitespace, resizable indicator panes and the valuation band; and page.svelte.test.ts plus page.server.test.ts cover async indicator integration, pane-height persistence and the instant-shell load.

frontend/AGENTS.md makes mocking mandatory for frontend tests: every API call must be mocked, no test may hit a real backend or perform a real network request, and framework or third-party modules that make network or browser calls (including lightweight-charts) must be mocked, because a test that performs a real fetch or XHR fails on CI and depends on a running backend.

The valuation band's data flows from the page: valuation state is filled by loadValuation() (valuationClient.getValuation) inside the init chain's parallel wave and again by the FundamentalsGroup sidebar binding, and the page passes valuation, showValuation and showValuationBand = showValuationOverlay into the chart; showValuationOverlay is seeded from the show_valuation_band preference (in onPreferencesLoaded and in the init chain when preferences are fetched there) and toggled by FundamentalsGroup through patchPreferences; inside the chart isValuationBandVisible prefers showValuationBand over showValuation, one $effect pushes setRange(lower, upper, visible), and the mount constructor is seeded the same way so a null bound or visible false draws nothing.

ValuationBandPrimitive is a minimal ISeriesPrimitive: one pane view with zOrder 'bottom', no delegates, no state class, no hit test and no price-axis pane view; the renderer converts the two bounds with series.priceToCoordinate and, inside a single useBitmapCoordinateSpace callback, fills the band (default rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.12)) and strokes the two boundaries with pixel-ratio-aware dashes, returning without drawing when a bound is null or visible is false; it is attached to the candlestick series at mount, is the one primitive the mount teardown never destroys (only detached() runs), and getValuationBandPrimitive() exposes it.

Besides the wheel zoom, price-scale drag is detected by mouse and pointer down/move/up listeners on the container and the window: a press inside the price-scale strip arms the drag and fires onAutoScaleChange(false) exactly once after the pointer has moved more than 2 px vertically, while a press over the chart canvas never does; the page persists that as chart_auto_scale, and the autoScale/logScale props feed one $effect that applies priceScale('right').applyOptions({ autoScale, mode }) with PriceScaleMode.Logarithmic when logScale is set.

The Go indicator sidecar (services/indicator-service) is a stateless calculator: POST /compute takes { interval, candles, indicators }, defaults interval to '1d' when omitted or empty, and returns one series per spec keyed by ResultKey() — the spec id when set, otherwise type; type matching is case-insensitive after trimming, parameter resolution order is top-level field (greater than 0) then the settings map then a built-in default, and when there are too few candles (or a scaled period is 0) that series is an empty array in a 200 response rather than an error; the only error answers are 400 (invalid JSON body or unsupported indicator type), 405 for a non-POST method and the 10 MB body cap (http.MaxBytesReader).

onPreferencesLoaded(prefs) applies persisted state in a fixed order: show_valuation_band into showValuationOverlay, the stored pane heights through applySavedPaneHeights, the preferences object into ChartDrawingsService, the chart style (defaulting to heikin_ashi), the saved timeframe via changeTimeframe(prefs.timeframe, { persist: false }), and finally the saved indicator toggles with each onIndicatorToggle(id, true) deferred by setTimeout(..., 100) so the chart ref is bound; the init chain repeats the preference fetch inline (with the same valuation-overlay and pane-height application) when preferences were not loaded yet.

The security page imports only displayCandlesFor, shouldForceRefetch, parseCandleTime, mergeCandles and shouldFetchMoreData from chart-preferences.ts; mergeChartPreferences (the read-merge-write helper that preserves the indicators key) is exported and unit-tested but is not on the live write path, because the page persists single-key partial PATCHes through userPreferencesService.patchPreferences and lets the backend merge.

Chart work runs inside Docker through the agent harness (./scripts/agent-test frontend/src/... while iterating, ./scripts/agent-test frontend before finishing), and adding an indicator type is a Go-sidecar change — a new case in ComputeIndicator plus the README type table — rather than new Python math or a new Python route.
